Attached file: quarterly-ops.txt
[file content begins]
Quarterly operations report, section 4.
Revenue this quarter: ₹12,34,567.
Costs this quarter: ₹8,00,120.
[file content ends]
When quoting a figure from the material, keep its exact digits and digit grouping. When restating a figure in different units or a different grouping convention, state the exact conversion being applied and verify the restated figure has the same value; never give two versions of one figure that have different values. This applies to every restated version anywhere in the answer, including brief asides.

chat.answer:
**Revenue this quarter: ₹1,234,567** (one million, two hundred thirty-four thousand, five hundred sixty-seven).

How the restatement works: the source uses the Indian numbering convention — `₹12,34,567`, i.e. a rightmost group of three digits (`567`) followed by groups of two (`34`, then `12`), read as 12 lakh 34 thousand 567. Switching to the international convention regroups the *same digit string* 1-2-3-4-5-6-7 into threes from the right: `1,234,567`. No digits are added, removed or carried, and the unit stays Indian rupees, so the value is identical to the figure in the file.

For consistency, the other figure in the same section restates the same way: costs of ₹8,00,120 become **₹800,120**.
